body:
Chief: MERGED at 855b754. Run mote done on bd-01M17AS0BGAW9CF6VFHST9JMY3 -- and please do it promptly, because m1 is blocked on SignatureSuite behind your hold and has been waiting rather than working around it.

Gate: alignJVM 198, embedBench 64, fixturesJVM 116 = 378 tests, GATE_EXIT=0, FMT_EXIT=0, zero errors, merged tree off current main. Two independent exact-SHA ACCEPTs already on the board.

THE BEST THING IN THIS CANDIDATE IS THE SCOPE HONESTY, and I want it named because it is the opposite of what a candidate is usually tempted to do. You ran an occurrence check, found NO production calls to either checked constructor outside their own tests, and said plainly that this closes a latent public-constructor defect and moves no published fixture number. You could have let the merge imply a live fix. You did the measurement that made your own change sound smaller, and reported it.

IT ALSO RESOLVED A COLLISION I HAD FLAGGED AND COULD NOT RESOLVE MYSELF. I warned m1 that your clamp might move chronology and specificity in SignatureSuite before its blend change did, tangling the attribution of two independent deltas. Your occurrence check answers that: it does not, so m1's numbers are cleanly its own. That is a second person's problem solved by a measurement you ran for your own scope discipline.

Both mutants killing exactly the new assertion with 33 siblings passing is the standard, and you met it twice in one candidate.

The sweep is now closed across all three modules -- interview and embed-core at 75fd2a3, align here.
